passage: In the packed, noisy library period, with the unit test ten minutes away, Raghavi should have been revising. Instead she watched Hemant across the table and made up a whole story: he was brilliant at cricket, kind to everyone and never angry. Then he snapped at the boy beside him for touching his pen, sulked, and knocked over his water bottle. Raghavi blinked. He was just a boy who got irritated and made a mess. Oddly, she liked that too. She did not think about changing her hair or her laugh for him. She turned back to her notes, and the daydream grew smaller while the real Hemant seemed more interesting.

qa.q: How much time was left before the unit test?
What did Raghavi think about Hemant at first, and what shook that picture?
qa.a: She imagined he was brilliant, kind and never angry, but seeing him snap over a pen and sulk showed her he had flaws.

qa.q: What does Raghavi do that shows a healthy way to hold a crush?
qa.a: She enjoys the feeling, notices the real Hemant with his flaws, and goes back to her revision instead of changing herself for him.

qa.q: How might Hemant see the moment when he snapped over the pen?
qa.a: Hemant was probably just irritated about his pen and had no idea anybody was building a perfect picture of him.

grounding: A child's idealised picture of her crush meets the real, imperfect boy, and she keeps enjoying the feeling without changing herself.

passage:
In her Vancouver classroom, Sofia spent all of maths daydreaming about Xin. He was perfect, she decided: kind, clever, funny, the best at basketball.
She even started pretending to like basketball, though she didn't.
Then one day in group work, Xin forgot his part of the project and shrugged it off. He also laughed at someone's wrong answer.
Sofia frowned. He wasn't perfect. He was just a regular boy.
She still liked him, a little. But she stopped pretending about basketball. She told the group she preferred drawing, and she'd do the poster.
It felt better being herself.

qa.q: What did Sofia pretend to like?
What was Sofia feeling while daydreaming about Xin?
qa.a: She felt dreamy and admiring, thinking he was perfect.

qa.q: What did Sofia notice that changed her view?
qa.a: That Xin forgot his part of the project and laughed at someone's wrong answer, so he wasn't perfect.

qa.q: How might Xin see Sofia offering to do the poster?
qa.a: Xin may see it as Sofia being helpful and good at drawing, without knowing about her crush.

grounding: A girl thinks her crush is perfect and daydreams in class, then sees his flaws, enjoys the feeling but stops changing herself to be liked.

passage:
At the badminton academy, Rukmini thought Raghav was the most perfect person in the world. Tall, fast, always smiling. She daydreamed about him during warm-ups and missed her drills.
She even started wearing her hair like the girls he talked to, though it kept falling in her eyes.
Then one day she saw Raghav throw his racket in anger after losing a match, and shout at his partner.
Rukmini blinked. He wasn't perfect after all.
She still liked him a little, but it felt more real now. And next practice she tied her hair her own way and focused on her drills.

qa.q: What did Raghav throw after losing a match?
How did Rukmini feel about Raghav at first?
qa.a: She felt dazzled and admiring, thinking he was perfect and daydreaming during warm-ups.

qa.q: What did Rukmini do after seeing Raghav's flaws?
qa.a: She kept her feelings but tied her hair her own way and focused on her drills.

qa.q: How might Raghav's partner feel after being shouted at?
qa.a: The partner was probably hurt and upset by Raghav's anger.

grounding: A girl idealises a boy at badminton and changes herself, then sees his real flaws, keeps a softer crush and goes back to being herself.
